name: recuperated_brayton_hthp
title: Recuperated Brayton high-temperature heat pump (air / HITEC molten salt)
summary: Steady design point of an air-cycle high-temperature heat pump delivering 1 MW to a molten-salt (HITEC) loop at 235-290 °C: compressor, gas-gas recuperator (cold-side effectiveness 0.94) and gas-to-salt exchanger with imposed terminal temperature differences; the pressure ratio is an output.

origin.source_path: main/standalone_base_recup_hthp.py (+ src/, src/input/ JSON specifications) in the repository below
origin.license: No LICENSE file in the original (README silent on licensing); credited and linked

verification.summary: The source was re-run in a Python venv (TESPy, repository commit fbc50b4): all state points, mass flows, powers and COP of the design case agree within 0.09 % (most below 0.05 %, same CoolProp air properties), and the Benvenuti validation variant agrees within 0.2 % on temperatures (0.02 % in K).
verification.reference: TESPy design-point rerun of main/standalone_base_recup_hthp.py (commit fbc50b4) and its stored results/tables; data/processed/Benvenuti_validation_recuperated.csv for the validation variant
verification.notes: Design case: COP 1.3288 vs 1.3291, P_2 1.4764 vs 1.476 bar, m_air 16.5937 vs 16.594 kg/s. Benvenuti variant: T_4 26.37 vs 26.32 °C (0.02 % in K), P_2 1.8821 vs 1.881 bar. The source's own validation against the Benvenuti reference data shows deviations up to 14 K (work in progress upstream); the CoolSolve model matches the TESPy rerun, not that reference.

related_external: TESPy (oemof/tespy), the Python library the source model is written in
